text:
ashok: Heads up — onboarding run for raven-liteq on canary pool showing intermittent JSON parse failures when function calls are retried. seen ~0.8% parse failures vs 0.02% baseline. stacktrace snippet attached.

maria: Ugh. did this start after the int8 quant build?

ashok: yep, after the latest qt1 patch. reproing locally with the mirror setup reproduces faster. looks like sometimes the toolcall payload is duplicated across retries and we end up with concatenated JSON fragments.

ashok: example log: `INVOKE id=abc123 attempt=1 payload:{"action":"lookup","args":{...}}` then retry: `INVOKE id=abc123 attempt=2 payload:{"action":"lookup","args":{...}}` but the streaming layer combined suffix of attempt1 with prefix of attempt2 -> `...}}{"action":` -> invalid JSON.

maria: are we seeing this only on streaming responses or also nonstreaming?

ashok: primarily streaming (v2 stream mode). non-streaming path seems fine. suspect kv cache / batching flush + tcp coalescing under small batches.

ashok: repro harness command I used: 
```
curl -sS -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"raven-liteq","input":"call tool foo"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

ashok: minimal script to flip retries/jitter to force concat: set retry_delay=0 and retry_jitter=0 in the client and send 10k quick low-latency requests.

maria: cc @dan @eva. this smells like a streaming chunk boundary / framing bug combined with retries. do we have per-invoke idempotency or delimiter protocol?

dan: we do have request_id forwarded but streaming backend doesn't currently insert an explicit delimiter between retry segments. it relies on JSON being self-contained.

eva: if the backend reuses the same connection and we do immediate retry it can reattach to existing chunk buffer. I think the quantized kernel introduced slightly different tokenization that can end a stream earlier, so the client thinks chunk complete and server starts next stream chunk without a clear separator.

maria: possible mitigations: 1) server add sentinel newline between attempts, 2) client enforce idempotency token and drop duplicate toolcall responses, 3) post-process stream to try NDJSON split and parse heuristics (best-effort recovery).

ashok: i can prototype server sentinel in a canary flag. quick patch: insert "\n---RETRY---\n" between retry payloads. will that break existing users? probably low risk for JSON-mode stream; but toolcall parsing expects pure JSON tokens.

dan: prefer less breaking: server could emit an event frame meta-line like `event: retry-boundary` using SSE framing (we already support SSE in hosted stream), and clients can ignore/handle.

maria: yeah SSE event frame is cleaner. failing that, we should add NDJSON wrapper so each attempt is a single line JSON, then stream consumer reads line-by-line.

eva: short-term hotfix: client-side parse heuristic: when JSON parsing fails, attempt to split on `}{` and `}
{` boundaries and try to reparse pieces. log the heuristics and increment telemetry counter. that should recover many cases without breaking protocol.

ashok: i already built a naive splitter — recovered ~60% of failures on sample. added log entry: `parse_repair_applied=1`. can push as a client lib patch and enable in canary.

maria: we also need to ensure retries aren't producing duplicate side-effects for tool providers. add idempotency header X-Invoke-Id and require tooling to dedupe by that id.

dan: agree. action items:
- dan: prototype SSE event frame server-side canary flag (eta 1d).
- ashok: land client parse-repair lib + enable in canary (eta 4h).
- eva: run a 100k request canary with retry jitter varied to estimate residual failure rate and measure duplicate tool invocations (eta 1d).
- maria: update rollout playbook to require idempotency header for tool integrators.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: raven-liteq/qt1-canary => host-group-canary at 2025-06-16T15:22:00Z (sha: f2a9c3).

maria: thanks. ashok — can you paste the client splitter snippet here so infra/devex can review?

ashok: snippet: 
```
function tryRepairStream(s) {
  try { return JSON.parse(s) }
  catch(e) {
    const parts = s.split(/}\s*\{/)
    for (let i=0;i<parts.length;i++) {
      let candidate = parts[i]
      if (i>0) candidate = '{'+candidate
      if (i<parts.length-1) candidate = candidate+'}'
      try { return JSON.parse(candidate) } catch(_) {}
    }
    throw e
  }
}
```

maria: nice. add telemetry tag and a backoff so this doesn't mask real regressions forever.

ashok: will do. enabling in canary now. pushing PR for client lib and a canary run report in #onboard-results when done.

eva: also create a small fuzz harness to append partial JSON fragments and test splitter edgecases.

dan: good. add a test that simulates TCP coalescing by concatenating frames with no separators.

maria: thanks team. once canary confirms <0.05% residual parse errors and no duplicate tool-side invocations, we can promote the fix.

ashok: acknowledged. starting canary run now.

maria: :thumbsup:
